scenes.heading: OPENAI'S *CHEAPEST* FRONTIER MODEL YET
scenes.say: OpenAI scrapped its last flagship, then shipped this one a day later at a fifth of the price. It is called GPT-6.1 Sol.

scenes.heading: TWO DOLLARS *PER MILLION*
scenes.label: output $10/M · cached $0.10/M · Astra was $10 in / $50 out
scenes.say: Two dollars per million input tokens, ten dollars out, and ten cents when the input is cached. That is about one fifth of Astra's pricing.
You can compare it with the rest of the family on the model page, and the playground is one click away.
scenes.heading: ONE PAGE, *EVERYTHING*
WHAT *TWO DOLLARS* BUYS
scenes.say: For that price: a context window of one point zero five million tokens, up to one hundred twenty eight thousand output tokens, reasoning effort up to max, and the tools — web search, computer use, and MCP.

scenes.title: API
scenes.heading: SIX TIMES *FASTER*, ONE FLAG
scenes.say: One flag — service tier ultrafast — and the same model answers six times faster. It is live now.

scenes.heading: THE *TRADE-OFFS*
scenes.say: The catches: no fine-tuning, inputs over two hundred seventy two thousand tokens cost twice as much, and there is no free tier. But cache hits cost ten cents, the context window is over a million tokens, and the ultrafast lane is live today.
Would you run your agents on it? Comment Sol and I will pin the model page.

youtube.title: GPT-6.1 Sol: OpenAI's Cheapest Frontier Model Yet
youtube.description:
GPT-6.1 Sol is OpenAI's new frontier model at $2 per 1M input and $10 per 1M output — about one fifth of what GPT-6.1 Astra would have cost. Cached input is $0.10/M; inputs over 272K tokens cost 2x input and 1.5x output. Context window: 1,050,000 tokens; max output 128k; reasoning effort up to max; tools include web search, computer use, code interpreter and MCP. No fine-tuning and no free tier. The Ultrafast service tier (6x speed) is live via service_tier=ultrafast.
Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.1-sol
